section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: Pushing an empty shopping trolley and a fully-loaded one with the same force produces very different accelerations — the loaded trolley speeds up far more slowly. This is best explained by which of Newton's Laws of Motion, which states that acceleration is directly proportional to the net force applied and inversely proportional to the object's mass?

options.option_text: Newton's Second Law of Motion (F = ma)
Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia)

explanation: Newton's Second Law (F = ma) directly relates force, mass, and acceleration — the loaded trolley has greater mass, so the same applied force produces smaller acceleration, distinct from the First Law (objects resist changes to their state of rest/motion without explaining the size of the change).

section: Science · Ch — Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: The law that states the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (voltage) across it, provided temperature remains constant — expressed as V = IR — is:
explanation: Ohm's Law (V = IR) governs the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in a conductor at constant temperature — distinct from Joule's Law (heating effect of current, H = I²Rt) or Faraday's Law (electromagnetic induction).

section: Science · Ch — Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: The loudness of a sound depends primarily on the ______ of the sound wave, while its shrillness (pitch) depends on the wave's frequency.
explanation: Loudness is governed by the amplitude of vibration (larger amplitude = louder sound), while pitch is governed by frequency (higher frequency = shriller/higher-pitched sound) — the two properties are independent of each other.
